subject: Post-call: LedgerLane economics & pilot next steps
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Ari Patel <ari.patel@ledgerlane.com>, Sofia Gomez <sofia.gomez@ledgerlane.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: LedgerLane economics & pilot next steps

Hi Ari / Sofia — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

What we heard
- Primary pain: latency-sensitive fraud screening at peak volumes (spikes up to 1.2M checks/day) causing timeouts and high cost per decision.
- Constraints: procurement budget capped for Q4 (~$75k), security requires VPC/network isolation for PII, and a short timeline to prove unit economics (~6 weeks).
- Goals: reduce per-decision inference cost 30%+ vs current baseline and keep median latency <150ms for 95th pct.

High-level economics (anchor from today’s notes)
- Baseline (no batching, hosted large model): token cost estimate ~$0.0035 per decision at current prompt sizes.
- Levers we recommended: continuous batching (40–60% token effective savings dependent on concurrency), KV/prefix caching for repeated context (10–25%), and model quantization (up to 25% CPU/GPU run-cost reductions in Dedicated).
- Combined anchor case: with batching + KV cache we expect ~30–45% reduction in token spend for typical fraud flows; exacts in the attached TCO workbook.

Recommended pilot (minimal friction, measurable ROI)
- 6-week pilot on Redwood Dedicated (reserved burst capacity) with:
  1) A focused traffic slice (2 endpoints, 10% of production traffic)
  2) Batching + KV cache preconfigured by our solutions team
  3) Weekly checkpoints + final TCO readout
- Why Dedicated for the pilot: gives deterministic latency and lets us demonstrate batch-density benefits. If procurement won’t approve a commit, we can run an equivalent scoped pilot hosted with SLO-backed fallbacks.

Attachments: LedgerLane_TCO-anchors.xlsx (detailed numbers) and redwood-pilot-sow-draft.pdf (pilot scope & responsibilities).

Action items (owners)
- Redwood: deliver updated TCO scenarios for 3 traffic profiles (Jasmine) — due Wed, Sep 1
- LedgerLane: confirm the two endpoint names and target 10% traffic slice (Ari) — due Tue, Aug 31
- Redwood Solutions: schedule kickoff with Karthik and assign infra lead (Marissa) — due Tue, Aug 31

Proposed follow-up: 30-min check on Thu 9/2 at 11am PT (I’ll send a calendar invite if that works).

Thanks — talk soon.

--

Thanks Jasmine — solid summary. A couple of quick clarifying Qs before we loop procurement: 

1) The 30–45% number: is that relative to our current hosted baseline (we’re on vendor X) or relative to a no-batching/no-cache run in your hosted offering?
2) On Dedicated vs hosted pilot: procurement is wary of commits. Is there a short-path where Redwood covers part of the pilot cost (credit) and we only commit if the readout meets the savings target?

Also can you add an example row in the TCO for a steady-state 1M decisions/month and a bursty scenario (daily peaks)? That will help the finance team.

—Ari

Subject: Re: Post-call: LedgerLane economics & pilot next steps

Great questions — quick answers inline.

On Mon, Aug 30, 2027 at 2:37 PM Ari Patel <ari.patel@ledgerlane.com> wrote:
> 1) The 30–45% number: is that relative to our current hosted baseline (we’re on vendor X) or relative to a no-batching/no-cache run in your hosted offering?

That figure is relative to a no-batching/no-cache run on the same model family (so it’s the marginal improvement you’d get from enabling batching + KV cache vs the naive run). If your current vendor has similar batching, the delta vs your baseline will be lower — I asked for any historical latency/throughput metrics you can share and will normalize the workbook to your vendor numbers once you send them.

> 2) Is there a short-path where Redwood covers part of the pilot cost (credit) and we only commit if the readout meets the savings target?

Yes — we typically offer a pilot credit structure for pilot commits. Proposed here: Redwood provides up to 10% pilot credit (applied to Dedicated reservation) and we jointly define a success metric (e.g., >=30% per-decision cost savings and P95 latency <150ms). If metrics are met, LedgerLane can choose to convert to a multi-month reserved capacity at the pre-agreed rate; if not met, we’ll take a post-mortem and share all telemetry.

I’ll add the 1M-decisions/month and burst scenarios to the TCO and push an updated workbook by EOD Wed (Sep 1). Karthik will prepare a short infra checklist for procurement (network/KMS requirements).

Proposed times for the 30-min follow-up: Thu 9/2 11am PT (preferred) or Fri 9/3 9am PT. Which works?

Thanks — Jasmine

--

- Jasmine: I’ll prepare a short internal approval note (we can offer pilot credit + Solutions SE time) for the enterprise team to sign off — need a one-paragraph justification and the success metric you proposed.

Also: scope a quick model-quantization experiment as an optional line item in the SOW — if we can show a 10–20% cost delta in lab, that makes the conversion ask easier.
